co_pocket_change_boulder.blurb: A single large sandstone boulder in the Sailing Hawks zone just outside Durango, sitting around 7,000 feet. Its features are huge huecos and pockets on vertical to overhanging faces, so the climbing leans powerful and sculpted. Ten problems are on record, running from around V2 up to V8, with a good middle band of V3 to V5 and a couple of hard test pieces. The north side tends to stay shaded while one overhanging east face picks up some morning sun. It sits on a short spur off the upper trail, past a talus field near the far west end, so expect a modest walk and a quiet session.

_expect.name: Chalk Creek Boulder aka Boulder of Sorrow

co_chalk_creek_boulder_aka_boulder_of_so.blurb: A lone granite boulder tucked in the trees in Chalk Creek Canyon, west of Buena Vista at roughly 9,000 feet. It is secluded and best known for tall problems, slab climbing and a dihedral line. Ten problems are recorded, mostly easy to moderate (V1 to V3) with a handful of harder ones reaching as high as V10, and several of the harder lines carry a serious landing. A short walk through the trees from the roadside pullout brings you to it, so it suits a quick stop with a few pads and a spotter rather than a full day.

co_highball_boulder.blurb: A boulder on Mount Herman above Monument, north of Colorado Springs, close to the area's main boulder and reached in well under a minute from it. As the name hints, the north and west sides hold the taller problems, while the east side has the harder, more technical ones. Ten problems are listed, spread from V1 to V6 with most in the V1 to V5 range, and the cracks and arete-style lines give it a varied feel. Bring plenty of pads and a spotter for the height. The surrounding hillside is secluded, with granite that is mostly good quality.

co_hilltop.blurb: A small cluster of boulders on the crown of the hill above the Moccasin Area near Nathrop, in the Buena Vista valley at about 8,300 feet. It is a short stroll up from the main boulders, so it pairs easily with a session there. The ten recorded problems include slab, arete and roof styles and run from V1 to about V6, with the bulk in the V3 to V5 range. Look for a blocky mini-roof as you climb the hill; more boulders sit on the very top and just down its west side. A good add-on stop for a mixed-ability group.

co_shadow_wall.blurb: A dark, prominent wall running along the ridgeline in Gateway Mesa Open Space, south of Denver near Castle Rock, sitting just above the Legacy Trail and part of the Shadow Realm cluster. It is bouldering only, with ten problems recorded at roughly V2 to V7. The spread skews hard, with several V6 and V7 lines and only a few easier warm-ups, so bring a handful of pads. The surrounding Shadow Realm is known for staying shaded all day, which helps on warm afternoons, and its rock suits slopey friction and crimps.

co_reese_s_pieces.blurb: A broken, west-facing rock band high above Campsite 5 and the Lincoln Creek dirt road, east of Aspen on the Independence Pass side, at roughly 11,000 feet. About ten routes mix trad and sport lines on granite, mostly in the 5.9 to 5.10 range with a few easier and one 5.11. The steep climb up through talus and aspens, ending at treeline below the cliff, takes 20 to 30 minutes, which helps keep it quieter than other crags nearby. Remote and scenic, with a high-alpine feel, so check afternoon weather and carry layers.
